definitions.explanation: Fruit that has been preserved by removing most of its water content through sun-drying or dehydration. Includes items such as raisins, dried persimmons, dried mangoes, and prunes.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦おやつ→おやつ：17921_oyatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I eat dried fruit as a snack.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{栄養|えいよう}→栄養：01882_eiyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{凝縮|ぎょうしゅく}→凝縮：17584_gyoushuku⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
グラノーラ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}や⟦ナッツ→ナッツ：11253_nattsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っていて→入る：00494_hairu⟧、⟦{朝食|ちょうしょく}→朝食：03122_choushoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ぴったり→ぴったり：02362_pittari⟧だ。
examples.english: Granola contains dried fruit and nuts, making it perfect for breakfast.

notes:
Composed of {干|ほ}し (dried, from the verb ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧) and ⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧ (fruit). In modern Japanese, the loanword ⟦ドライフルーツ→ドライフルーツ：20795_doraifuruutsu⟧ is very commonly used alongside the native term. {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの} tends to evoke traditional Japanese dried fruits like ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧ (dried persimmon), while ⟦ドライフルーツ→ドライフルーツ：20795_doraifuruutsu⟧ often refers to imported or Western-style products.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make dried fruit
- {干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}{入|い}り: containing dried fruit
- ⟦{無添加|むてんか}→無添加：19283_mutenka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{干|ほ}し{果物|くだもの}: additive-free dried fruit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ドライフルーツ→ドライフルーツ：20795_doraifuruutsu⟧: dried fruit — the loanword equivalent; more common in commercial contexts
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧: dried persimmon — a traditional Japanese dried fruit
- ⟦{乾物|かんぶつ}→乾物：06191_kanbutsu⟧: dried goods — a broader category including dried vegetables, seaweed, and mushrooms
